 India weather VAR twists to reach SAFF final
 Published : 14 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 14 November 2026, 21:22
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 Photo: Firoz Ahmed 
 Despite two significant VAR decisions going against them, defending champions India reached the SAFF Championship final after the nine-time champions battled past Bhutan 2-1 in the first semifinal at the National Stadium on Saturday. 
 India will now feature in Tuesday's final, their 14th appearance in the title decider in 15 editions, against the winners of the other semifinal between hosts Bangladesh and their opponents. 
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Image 
 Indian coach Naushad Moosa made six changes to the side that beat Maldives 1-0, and India dominated from the outset, taking a 2-0 lead inside the half-hour mark. However, Bhutan produced another spirited second-half performance, as they had against Sri Lanka, to pull a goal back and came close twice to forcing an equaliser in stoppage time. Their fightback, though, was not enough to secure a maiden final berth.
 Vishnu Puthiya Valappil, capitalising on a long ball from the halfway line, nutmegged Nima Wangdi before driving a low shot past goalkeeper Gyeltshen Zangpo to give India the lead in the ninth minute. Captain Chinglensana Singh then volleyed home a Manglenthang Kipgen corner in the 27th minute to double their advantage.
 Image 
 Bhutan came out with renewed purpose after the break and took control for much of the second half, reducing the deficit just three minutes after the restart. Kingzang Tashi Tobden's strike was initially ruled out for offside by the assistant referee, but the decision was overturned following a VAR review, with the technology operated from Thailand.
 India also had a penalty decision overturned after Indonesian referee Alkatiri Thoriq Munir reviewed the incident on the pitchside VAR monitor, allowing Bhutan to escape a spot-kick.
 India could have restored their two-goal cushion in the 84th minute, but Suhail Ahmed Bhat was denied by the crossbar. Bhutan then threatened twice in stoppage time. Substitute Kinzang Tenzin's low drive from inside the box was comfortably gathered by India goalkeeper Arsh Anwer Shaikh before the forward failed to connect with a promising header, as Bhutan's dream of reaching their first final fell short.
 Image 
 India had previously won the SAFF Championship with their U-23 side in 2009 and finished runners-up with a second-string team in 2018. Both tournaments were held in Dhaka.
